title: Income tax reassessment - the time limits after recent legal changes
p1:
Can the Income Tax Department reopen your tax assessment even after several years?

Yes, but there is a legal deadline. And recent changes have significantly altered the rules that taxpayers and professionals need to know.
p2:
A common misconception is that the tax department can reopen any old assessment whenever it discovers a discrepancy.

That is not correct. The deadline depends on the applicable law, the relevant tax year and the amount of income believed to have escaped assessment.

Under the Income-tax Act, 1961, amended rules effective from September 1, 2024, generally allow reassessment notices within 3 years and 3 months. This can extend to 5 years and 3 months where escaped income is ₹50 lakh or more.
p3:
There is another major development: the Income-tax Act, 2025, came into effect on April 1, 2026.

For tax years beginning from April 1, 2026, the new rules generally allow 4 years and 3 months for reassessment notices, extending to 6 years and 3 months where escaped income is ₹50 lakh or more.

The crucial takeaway? Earlier tax years generally remain governed by the old Act, while new tax years follow the 2025 Act. The applicable deadline must be checked before accepting a reassessment notice as valid.
conclusion: Have you ever received an income tax reassessment notice for an older financial year? Do you think the revised time limits offer taxpayers better protection? Share your thoughts.
